items.title: Pricing a structured note
items.prompt: A desk issues $q$ thousand units of a structured note. The price per unit falls with volume: $\text{£}(50 - q)$. Each unit costs £10.00 to issue, and fixed costs are £300 thousand. (a) Write the profit $P$, in £ thousands, as a quadratic in $q$. (b) Find the break-even volumes by factorising. (c) Complete the square to find the profit-maximising volume, the price there and the largest profit. (d) Can the desk make £120 thousand? Can it make £75 thousand? Use the discriminant, and give the volumes where possible. Give a reason for each step.
items.model:
**(a) Profit.** Revenue is price times volume, $q(50 - q)$. Costs are $10q + 300$. So

$$\begin{aligned} P &= q(50 - q) - 10q - 300 \\ &= -q^2 + 40q - 300. \end{aligned}$$

**(b) Break-even.** Set $P = 0$:

$$\begin{aligned} -q^2 + 40q - 300 &= 0 \\ &\quad \text{break-even means} \\ &\quad \text{zero profit} \\ q^2 - 40q + 300 &= 0 \\ &\quad \text{multiply by } -1 \\ (q - 10)(q - 30) &= 0 \\ &\quad 10 \times 30 = 300, \\ &\quad 10 + 30 = 40 \\ q &= 10 \ \text{or}\ q = 30 \\ &\quad \text{a zero product needs} \\ &\quad \text{a zero factor} \end{aligned}$$

The desk breaks even at 10 thousand and 30 thousand units.

**(c) Maximum.** Complete the square on $q^2 - 40q$:

$$\begin{aligned} q^2 - 40q &= (q - 20)^2 - 400 \\ &\quad \text{half of } -40 \text{ is } -20 \\ P &= -\big((q - 20)^2 - 400\big) - 300 \\ &\quad \text{substitute} \\ P &= 100 - (q - 20)^2 \\ &\quad \text{simplify} \end{aligned}$$

A square is never negative, so $P$ is largest when $q = 20$: £100 thousand. The price there is $50 - 20 = $ £30.00 a unit. The peak sits halfway between the break-evens, 10 and 30.

**(d) Targets.** Profit $T$ is reachable when $q^2 - 40q + (300 + T) = 0$ has a real root.

For $T = 120$: $q^2 - 40q + 420 = 0$ has $b^2 - 4ac = 1600 - 1680 = -80 < 0$. No volume works, which agrees with the maximum of £100 thousand.

For $T = 75$: $q^2 - 40q + 375 = 0$ has $b^2 - 4ac = 1600 - 1500 = 100 > 0$. So $q = \tfrac{40 \pm 10}{2}$: 15 thousand or 25 thousand units. Check: $-225 + 600 - 300 = 75$.

For £120 thousand: forms $q^2 - 40q + 420 = 0$, finds the discriminant −80 and concludes it is impossible.
For £75 thousand: finds the discriminant 100 and the volumes 15 thousand and 25 thousand units, with a check.
